earlier_scan.source_named: Not covered in Tryon 1974 (PL C-32, read); Glottolog lists only kinship/ethnographic works (Falkenberg 1962, 1981) and wordlists.

sources.citation: Green, Ian. 1989. Marrithiyel: a language of the Daly River region of Australia's Northern Territory. PhD thesis, ANU. http://hdl.handle.net/1885/10926
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 1.4 (dialects) names only Marridan, Marri Ammu and Marrisjabin as Marrithiyel dialects and Marengar/Maranunggu as 'close' neighbours; Mariyedi never mentioned. Stress section 2.1.3 pp. 33-39 (stem-initial primary stress) is about Marrithiyel, not Mariyedi.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1974. Daly family languages, Australia. Pacific Linguistics C-32. Canberra: ANU. 305 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No token Marijedi/Mariyedi/Murijadi/Marijadi anywhere in the scanned text (language-name tally covers Marithiel, Marityaben, Maridan, Marimanindji, Maringar, Maridyerbin, Mariwumiri); the book has no word-stress/accent statement for any language (all 'stress' hits are the sense 'emphasise').

sources.citation: AIATSIS. AUSTLANG dataset (CSV export), row N164 'Mariyedi' (synonyms Marijedi, Murijadi, Marijadi; -13.721, 130.051; NT).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identifier record only. The full AUSTLANG N164 page (documentation scores, holdings) is behind an automated-access block JS wall and could not be opened.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Compiles Moseley 2007, Ethnologue 16 and World Oral Literature Project only; no other sources; nothing linguistic. (Live page could not be reached by automated download; 2023 Internet Archive copy.)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid records mari1423 (Mariyedi) and mari1420 (Marithielic). https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/mari1423
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification Western Daly [west2434] > Bringen [brin1245] > Marithielic [mari1420]; Glottolog's most extensive descriptions all 'a wordlist or less' (Moseley 2007, Tindale 1974, Falkenberg 1962); 'Comments on subclassification: Tryon 1974'. Zero descriptive references.

sources.citation: Green, Ian & Rachel Nordlinger. 2022. The Daly Languages (Australia): 'Language Relationships' and 'Resources' pages. ARC CoEDL. https://www.dalylanguages.org/historical.php
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Western Daly listed as Marramaninjsji, Marranunggu, Emmi, Menthe, Marri Ngarr, Magati Ke, Marri Tjevin, Marri Ammu, Marri Dan, Marrithiyel; no variety called Mariyedi/Marri Yedi anywhere on the site (resources list Ian Green's field notes/recordings for Marrithiyel, Marri Tjevin, Magati Ke, Marri Ngarr, etc.). Typology page 'under construction'; no stress statements.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th ed. Dallas: SIL. Entry 'Mariyedi' [zmy].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Population 20 (Wurm & Hattori 1981); 'Inland from Anson Bay, south of Manda, southwest of Darwin'; Australian, Daly, Bringen-Wagaydy, Bringen; 'Nearly extinct'. No linguistic content. (2010 Internet Archive copy.)

sources.citation: Moseley, Christopher (ed.). 2007. Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages. London: Routledge. Entry 'Mariyedi [230]', pp. 515-516.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Entry gives only location (southwest of Darwin, south of Manda), classification Daly, Bringen-Wagaydy, Bringen, 'For structural information see the Jawoyn entry', c. 20 speakers in 1981, moribund. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Green, Ian. 1981. The phonology and morphology of Marrithiyel: a preliminary study. MA thesis, ANU. http://hdl.handle.net/1885/11089
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent all Mariyedi spellings: no mention. Stress section 2.3 concerns Marrithiyel only.

sources.citation: Tindale, Norman B. 1974. Aboriginal tribes of Australia. Berkeley: UC Press. Catalogue entry 'Marijedi (NT)' as transcribed by South Australian Museum Archives, Tindale's Catalogue of Australian Aboriginal Tribes (updated 5 June 2019).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic only: location west of Mount Greenwood toward Cape Scott, 129°55'E x 13°45'S, 500 sq km; references Falkenberg 1948, 1962; Stanner 1970 MS; alt. names Murijadi (used by Murinbata), Marijadi. Nothing on language or stress. (Live samuseum site refused connection; downloaded via web.archive.org.)

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Western Daly languages' and 'Mariyedi language' (redirects to Marrithiyel).
sources.note: Western Daly page lists Maranunggu, Marrithiyel (dialects Marri Ammu, Marritjevin, Marridan, Marramanindjdji), Marri Ngarr (Magati-ge); no Mariyedi. 'Mariyedi language' redirects to the Marrithiyel article (Green 1981 cited); nothing on stress there.
